correctness.rationale: For a fixed received-length change δ, a shorter removal window can be extended to d=min(k,k−δ) on the input and padded with the unchanged letters on the corresponding sides of the inserted block. Such a containing window always exists since n≥k, including insertions at the ends. If i=d+δ>0, an output at a nonfinal position j has a later representation exactly when its first inserted symbol equals x_j: later positions preserve x_j, and matching it permits a shift by one and appending x_(j+d). Thus each nonfinal window contributes (q−1)q^(i−1) distinct rightmost representatives and the final one q^i. At δ=−k, deletion outputs at a<b agree exactly when x_j=x_(j+k) throughout a≤j<b; the outputs count equal runs. The k nontrivial nonpositive offsets sum to the geometric part of A, and δ=1,…,k gives the displayed arithmetic part. Along the residue-class paths there are q^k root assignments and exactly q−1 child choices for each edge designated unequal (one for each equal edge). This gives the full histogram, binomial law, all extrema and moments; n=k is degenerate and the normal limit only standardizes positive variance as n−k→∞ at fixed q. Exact replay in /workspace/review-replay.py (argument 1) independently built deduplicated outputs as strings and checked all layers, the closed-form baseline and entire center histogram on 44 triples and 17,413 centers; the symbolic argument supplies the unrestricted theorem. Minimum centers are precisely words having k as a period in the finite-word sense, not necessarily having least period dividing k.

evidence: Theorem 1's bracket (q−1)(n−t+1)+1 equals q+(n−t)(q−1). With (t,s)=(k,k+δ) for −k<δ≤0 or (k−δ,k) for δ>0 this is exactly the frozen formula. At δ=−k the known deletion formula adds one per mismatch x_j≠x_(j+k).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Writing an edit as a maximal-pair edit needs only extension with unchanged letters; disjoint output lengths are then summed. For each designated set of j mismatches there are q^k(q−1)^j words by the sequential choices of letters. Summing over the binomial number of sets proves every population count and the displayed law. The mean, variance and normal limit are immediate binomial consequences. No new obstruction or invariant survives this implication.

originality.rationale: The frozen comparison misses the arbitrary-alphabet fixed-pair theorem of Sun, Lu, Zhang and Ge (arXiv:2403.11750v2, Theorem 1), not just the earlier binary formula. It covers exactly the two claimed positive-insertion shell counts after a one-step window-padding reduction. The only exceptional shell is the already published burst-deletion size formula. Its random-center law is obtained directly by freely choosing the first k letters and choosing at each subsequent position either the letter k places back (one choice) or any other letter (q−1 choices). Disjoint lengths then give the displayed binomial histogram without another counting problem. The complete aggregate was not located verbatim; the failure is straightforward implication from existing exact results, not a claim of verbatim prior publication or of incorrect formulas.
residual_risks: A verbatim aggregate distribution may also exist under a different name. The rejection does not depend on locating it.
The founder paper of Tang et al. is identified by Ye–Ge but its full text was not examined; the cited exact fixed-burst and deletion results suffice for the coverage decision.

value.rationale: The error-ball distribution is a natural diagnostic, but this version writes out a direct aggregation of the known arbitrary-q fixed-burst formula and pure-deletion count. Padding determines the representative pair with no new overlap enumeration; the binomial law is immediate sequential counting once the deletion count is inserted. The result is useful as a summary of existing facts, but no nonmechanical exact gap remains and no independent code-size or inverse-ball result is proved. There is no substantive repair in the frozen scope.
